> [!WARNING]
> **Pre-release — for personal testing only.** This build is meant for trying out the functionality yourself, not for rolling out to your clients. Stability is still poor, and updates will be frequent and breaking. If you need something dependable, wait for the `0.1.0` release.

Third ReClash pre-release. The same cross-platform proxy client built on the mihomo core, for Android, Windows, macOS and Linux. The headline since `pre.2` is in-app updates: the client now finds and installs new builds on its own. It also reworks the connection doctor and the smart-routing engine.

## What's new since pre.2

- In-app updates: the client checks for new builds itself. It reads the releases list with a channel policy — a prerelease build always steps onto the finished stable release, a stable build picks up prereleases only when you enable the new **Prerelease updates** toggle, and the highest eligible version always wins. (Builds up to `pre.2` cannot see this yet, so update to `pre.3` by hand once; the client takes over from there.)
- Connection doctor: technical details move to their own tab. The standard check now runs only from the app-bar refresh, the run button names the selected depth, and flush and export become quiet rows.
- Smart routing: ranking, switching, and reporting share one park-scaled measured latency; discovery probes the closest nodes first; and a live, reaching session is never flipped onto a home or distrusted exit.

## Fixes since pre.2

- Layout: a phone in landscape keeps the mobile layout (decided by the shortest side), and a window resize no longer force-closes dialogs, sheets, or the setup wizard.

<!-- reclash:release-epoch:1 -->

## Notice

Out of the box this build identifies itself to subscription servers with the `FlClashX/v0.4.2` User-Agent, so existing provider panels keep serving clash configs. That header is the default preset, not the only option: you can pick another client identity in settings. Thanks to the [FlClashX](https://github.com/pluralplay/FlClashX) project, whose header ReClash borrows for compatibility until panels recognize its own identity.
